## A new look

- STL Editor has a fresh, darker look that's easier on the eyes. Prefer it light? View › Theme › Light (or Match Windows).
- The model now fills the whole window. The Browser floats at the top left, a tool's settings open at the top right, and the History bar runs along the bottom.
- The toolbar is tidier: tabs are rounded buttons, each group's name sits under its tools, and a ⌄ under a group name lists its tools. Search for any tool from the box at the top right (or press Ctrl+K).
- Tool panels keep the everyday settings at the top. The rest fold away in sections you open with a click, and the panel remembers which ones you left open. A closed section says "2 changed" if you changed something inside it.

## A simpler Support Fins panel

- Two cards at the top tell you what matters: how much of the overhang is **Held**, and how much **Support plastic** the fins add.
- Rotate, Add fins and Remove fins sit in one row under the part's name.
- Placement and Setup are showing. Tines, Clearances, Sway braces and Walls fold away until you need them.
- *Add as*, the filament for the plastic estimate and *Bare beyond* are now in the **Output** section.
- Draw Walls has the same tidy layout.

## Fixes

- The Held line could show an error on a part with nothing to hold up. It now says "Nothing to hold up".
- If a mesh failed to open, your open project could be emptied, and the next save could overwrite it. Now nothing changes when an open fails.
- Undo right after opening a mesh in the web edition no longer empties the window.
- After a crash or an update restart, recovered projects keep their parameters, so steps that use them keep working.
- Simplify and Repair work on very big meshes again. They stopped with an error on meshes of a few hundred thousand triangles.
- A long job, like a fine Hollow or a big Support Fins build, no longer makes the app close itself when it runs in a browser window.
- A formula with too many numbers, like `round(x, 1)`, now says what's wrong instead of stopping the app from updating.
- Dragging the Support Fins rings twice in quick succession no longer turns the part twice.
- Clicking a body in the Browser while placing holes no longer puts a hole in the middle of nowhere.
- Old fins and suggestions no longer come back after you change the part while they're still being worked out.
- With a section view on, you can click and measure the surfaces inside the cut.
- Smoother when you sketch and work for a long time: the app frees memory it no longer needs.
- The web edition's autosave only saves when something changed, so it no longer slows you down on big projects.
- Clicking a face on a big mesh in the web edition is faster.
- Other websites can't send commands to the desktop app.
